title: Nine Rows and One Cough
subtitle: 戏剧表演 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）
meta: 主题语境：戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）　|　核心词汇：audience　|　正文 328 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 audience 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the ① audience was nine people and a dog, and my aunt said that was the best audience she ever had. The ② audience, meaning the people and not the number, sat in the first nine rows and moved there together; an audience, she said, is the only crowd that has agreed to be quiet. She said a crowd that has not agreed is a different animal entirely.

Every ③ audience in that hall coughed at the same place, and she said you could set a clock by it. Their ④ audience on the Thursday gave nine seconds of applause and one silence; an audience, my father said, is the only judge that announces its verdict before it has heard the case. He said the silence was the verdict.

My grandfather used the word the other way and meant ⑤ an audience with somebody important, which he had once, in 1951, for nine minutes. The ⑥ audience, meaning the formal meeting and not the crowd, is the only word that covers both a theatre and an office; an audience, he said, is either a room full of people or one person with a diary. He said the diary is the harder one.

By 1969 the ⑦ audience had grown to ninety and the coughing had stopped, which she said was worse. The ⑧ audience she wanted was the nine people, because they had come on purpose; an audience, my mother said, is the only thing that gets worse as it gets bigger and better as it gets smaller. She said ninety people is a crowd and nine is a jury.

The ⑨ audience I remember is the one on the Thursday, nine rows of them, who clapped in the wrong place. An ⑩ audience, my aunt said in 1974, is the only person that everybody is performing for and nobody has met; every audience, she said, is one mind made out of people who disagree. She said the mind is wrong about eleven times a night.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 观众；听众（一场的观众）
B. n. 观众（指那些人，与人数相对）
C. n. 观众（指星期四那一场）
D. 固定搭配：an audience of nine people 九个人的观众
E. 固定搭配：an audience with somebody 会见、觐见
F. n. 接见；会见（抽象）
G. n. 观众（指她想要的、九个人的那种）
H. n. 观众（抽象总称；泛指）

items.q: the audience was nine people and a dog
The audience, meaning the people and not the number
The audience, meaning the formal meeting
the audience had grown to ninety
An audience, my aunt said in 1974

answers.why: an audience of nine people 意为“九个人的观众”，1966 年的观众是九个人加一条狗，姑姑说那是她有过的最好的观众。
audience 指“那些人”，与人数相对，观众坐在前九排，而且是大家一起挪过去的。
audience 意为“观众”，那个礼堂里每一场观众都在同一个地方咳嗽，她说你可以拿它对表。
audience 意为“观众”，他们星期四那场观众给了九秒钟掌声和一段沉默。
an audience with somebody 意为“会见、觐见”，祖父说的是另一回事：1951 年他有过一次要人的接见，历时九分钟。
audience 意为“接见、会见（抽象）”，与人群相对，它是唯一既指剧院又指办公室的词。
audience 意为“观众”，到 1969 年观众增加到九十人，咳嗽却停了，她说那更糟。
audience 指她想要的、九个人的那种观众，因为她要的观众是那九个人，他们是专程来的。
audience 指星期四那一场，我记得的是星期四那九排观众，他们在错的地方鼓了掌。
audience 为抽象总称，泛指“观众这种东西”，姑姑说观众是所有人都在为它表演、却谁也没见过的那一个人。
